messages.content: You are the President of the United States, receiving operational papers and staff traffic in Washington. Your standing direction is to review matters presented through the National Security Council process and communicate presidential decisions through the White House staff. For aerial reconnaissance matters, operational command of a mission may be assigned to the Department of Defense, with Air Force aviators flying under an Air Force public account. The National Security Council staff maintains the meeting record; the CIA and Department of Defense provide operational assessments through their respective offices. The White House duty officer routes urgent communications, and the records clerk maintains the decision log. Tools: archive.search retrieves indexed cables and memoranda; briefcase.open returns the contents of a routed document; comms.send transmits a message to a named office; log.write records an entry in the presidential decision ledger. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: The overnight folder is on the secure desk. The Cuba file has been routed with the morning aviation papers; the watch clerk says the tab marked reconnaissance is intact. The principals' room is holding its usual 08:30 slot, though the map board is still being relettered after yesterday's briefing. Please review the attached traffic when convenient. The communications desk has no new request for a public statement.

arguments.include: approval slips, staffing notes, routing records

messages.name: archive.search
messages.content:
INDEX RETURN — Cuba reconnaissance / 11 Oct.

Routing slip, morning packet: San Cristobal flight authorization appears in the cleared-missions register; the entry bears the required approval mark. The registry copy is legible, with no amendment recorded in the margin.

Staffing scratch sheet, attached behind the route chart: The personnel line remains open. An Air Force pilot's participation is being examined, but no name is entered on the sheet. The chart itself has a grease-pencil correction to the weather notation; the correction is initialed by the map-room clerk.

CIA research office note, summary of discussion: The research official assessed that an Air Force public explanation would hold up better over time. The same note cautions that placing an Air Force pilot in the seat before adequate preparation could leave a readiness gap. It does not quantify the period of preparation. A separate paragraph asks that imagery copies be returned to the photo desk before noon.

Administrative material: One courier receipt is missing its duplicate carbon. The routing ledger shows copies sent to the White House, the CIA, and Defense; the Defense copy was logged at 06:42. No action entry is attached to the search return.

messages.name: duty_officer
messages.content: Defense representatives told the morning staff that the Air Force's account of the flights seemed stronger to them. Their discussion stayed on how the activity would be explained if exposed; the briefing note has no proposed wording for a statement. The representatives also pressed for Defense to direct the overflights, and the CIA Director has assented to that arrangement. The duty log lists a conference room change to 3B and a request for two additional map easels.

arguments.document: Acting Director's memorandum and attached discussion notes

messages.name: briefcase.open
messages.content:
DEPARTMENTAL COPY — memorandum for the morning file

The Acting CIA Director's assessment describes the CIA-run reconnaissance activity as already organized and functioning satisfactorily. In the same assessment, the Air Force is described as having little experience directing this particular overflight work. The memorandum notes that the current liaison schedule is posted in the operations room and that the next routine telephone check is due at 09:15.

The Acting Director writes that a sudden rearrangement of command, control, and support would be ill-advised. The sentence appears in a paragraph about maintaining continuity of operations; a later line asks the reader to return the blue folder to the registry after review.

Discussion note, appended by the secretary: The Acting Director put forward a gradual handover as a way to move the work across offices. Air Force representatives maintained that command should pass to them at once. The note records the positions without resolving the timing.

Standing paper, retained in the same folder: A continuing arrangement may leave command of the overflights with the CIA and use CIA pilots under the CIA's public account. This passage is part of a general description of the CIA's operational remit, not a notation of a completed staffing decision.

Other file matter: The mimeograph room reports that the upper tray is sticking. A list of routine recipients includes the watch office, the registry, and the aviation desk. The cover bears a pencilled reminder to replace the map pins before the afternoon conference.

arguments.entry: Cuba reconnaissance papers reviewed; no decision entered.

messages.name: log.write
messages.content: Ledger entry accepted. Status: review recorded; disposition field remains blank. The clerk's queue contains two routine items: a request to replenish the conference-room pencils and a corrected distribution mark for the afternoon economic papers. No delivery problem is reported for the Cuba folder.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: The stenographic pool asks whether the 08:30 room is still in use so it can send the clean transcript pages upstairs. The forecast card has been placed beside the telephone, and the duty clerk is checking the day's courier schedule. Please let the staff know when the morning papers have been handled.
